INTRODUCTIONThe lecture introduces general information about the Vietnam People's Army, including: history of formation and development, structure and organization; forces under the Ministry of Defense.II. TEXT1. History of formation and development of the Vietnam People's Army.Under the directive  of  President Ho Chi Minh and the command of comrade Vo Nguyen Giap, the Viet Nam Proganda Unit of the Liberation Army, the forerunner of the Vietnam People’s Army (VPA), was founded on the basis of revolutionary armed teams in Viet Bac on 22 December 1944 in Nguyen Binh district, Cao Bang province.Nowadays, the Vietnam People’s Army has been built as an Army for combat, active work and production as well as a regular, elite, more and more modern Army to successfully perform its mission of defending the country, contributing actively and effectively to the cause of building up the country.         The Establishment Ceremony of the Viet Nam Propaganda Unit of Liberation Army (22 December 1944) was held in Tran Hung Dao Forest (Nguyen Binh district, Cao Bang province).Source: 2019 Vietnam National Defence 2. Organisation of the Viet Nam People’s ArmyThe VPA comprises the Main Force and Local Force, military regions, services, the Border Guard, army corps and arms, a system of logistical support units, technical support units, military academies, officer training schools, research institutes, and economic-defence units.2.1. Ground ForcesThe Ground Forces consist of seven military regions (1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, and 9) and Ha Noi Capital High Command, four army corps (1, 2, 3, and 4) and six arms (Commando, Artillery, Tank and Armour, Engineering, Signal, and Chemical).The Ground Forces of Viet Nam are equipped in the modern direction so as to achieve the capabilities of high mobility, strong offensive capabilities and firepower, and fighting in various terrains, in all weathers in conformity with the art of modern people’s war. At present, Viet Nam has produced and put into service a number of relatively modern infantry weapons.Ground Forces2.2. Air Defence-Air ForceThe Air Defence-Air Force assumes the responsibilities for both national air defence and air force. It is the core force responsible for the control and defence of the airspace, protection of the nation’s critical facilities and the people, and participates in safeguarding seas and islands of the Homeland. The service plays the role of a consultative organ for the Ministry of National Defence on matters concerning the building of the air defence of the Ground Forces and other service and arms air forces,… Parachute training at the 916 th Regiment, 371th Division, the Air Defence-Air Force.2.3. NavyThe Viet Nam People’s Navy is the core service in protecting sovereignty, sovereign rights, territorial unity and integrity of Viet Nam’s seas and islands and building the national defence posture at sea. The Navy has responsibility to manage and firmly defend the sea waters and islands under Viet Nam’s sovereignty, ready for combating independently or participating in combined operations to defeat any aggression at sea. It is also responsible for maintaining security, countering any acts of violating sovereignty, sovereign rights, jurisdiction and national interests of Viet Nam at sea, and participating in disaster prevention and relief, and search and rescue, securing economic production and other normal activities in Viet Nam's sea waters and islands in conformity with Vietnamese and international laws. The 3rd Naval Region conducting Zone 1 joint combat exercise2.4. Border GuardBorder Guard on their dutyThe Border Guard is the people's armed force of the Communist Party of Vietnam and the State of the Socialist Republic of Viet Nam, constitutes part of the VPA, and plays a core and specialized role in managing and protecting the sovereignty, territorial integrity, security and order of the national borders on land, seas, islands and border gates according to its tasks prescribed by law. It is also a force component in the border provincial and district defence zones. The Border Guard exercises its functions in accordance with the laws of the Socialist Republic of Viet Nam and international conventions, of which the Socialist Republic of Viet Nam is a signatory, related to sovereignty, security of the national borders on land, seas, islands and border gates. 2.5. Cyber CommandCyber Command Force in their missionThe Cyber Command is a combat component of the VPA. It plays a core role in defending national sovereignty in cyberspace, countering information warfare, cyberwarfare and safeguarding the Homeland in cyberspace. It is also an important force which participates in protecting national critical information systems, ensuring information network safety, protecting national network security and countering "peaceful evolution" in cyberspace, contributing to the entire Party, people and military's effort to firmly defend the independence, sovereignty, unity and territorial integrity of the Homeland. 2.6. Viet Nam Peacekeeping DepartmentViennam Peacekeeping Force on the way to executed the missionViet Nam Peacekeeping Department (previously known as Viet Nam Peacekeeping Centre) is under the direct leadership of the Ministry of National Defence. It is the advisory organ for the Central Military Commission, Minister of National Defence, and the Steering Board of the Ministry of National Defence on the leadership, command, and operation of the VPA's forces participating in the United Nations peacekeeping operations. It also takes charge of the management, command and operation of the whole process of preparation and participation in the United Nations peacekeeping operations and assists the Minister of National Defence in performing the state management of the VPA's United Nations peacekeeping operations.2.7. Local ForceThe Local Force is a component of the people’s three-category armed forces and is organised in provinces, cities, towns and districts. It is a core force in the local people’s war, a mobile force engaging in operations mainly in the designated local area, coordinating and working with the Militia and Self-Defence Force, people's public security force in operations, and maintaining the local political security in peacetime2.8. ReserveThe Reserve is a component of the VPA and an important force, contributing to the building of the all-people national defence and the people's war posture. It is ready to supplement the active force when required, meeting the demands of building and safeguarding the socialist Vietnamese Homeland in the new situation. Drill with gun training at army unit2.9. Academies, Colleges and SchoolsParticipate in the Opening of the Army Day of Books and Reading Culture in 2023The VPA has a complete system of academies, colleges and schools to meet the demands for training officers and non-commissioned officers as well as technicians at all levels for the VPA, postgraduates and civilian technicians. Those institutions also conduct scientific and technological research in the VPA, foster all kinds of learners on defence and security knowledge, educate and further advance political theoretical knowledge. The Ministry of National Defence directly administers the National Defence Academy, Political Academy, Army Academy, Logistics Academy, Military Technology Academy, the 1st Army Officer Training College, the 2nd Army Officer Training College, and the Political Officer Training College. 2.10. Major Research InstitutesMajor Research Institutes consist of: The Institute for Defence Strategy, The Institute of Military Social Sciences and Humanities, The Institute for Military Science and Technology, Viet Nam Institute for Military History, The Institute for Defence International Relations”.Academy of Military Science and Technology2.11. Major Economic-Defence UnitsEconomic-defence units of the VPA are the leading force in combining economic development with national defence and security consolidation. The VPA’s groups, corporations and economic-defence corps have made considerable contributions to the cause of industrialization and modernization of the country, playing the role of a key force in the most difficult regions, participating in local socio-economic development, thus creating strong and stable national defence posture in the vital areas of the Homeland.The commanders visited military factoriesIII. UNIT 2: UNIFORMSI. INTRODUCTION The Military uniform of the Vietnam People's Army is a system of costumes for soldiers and officers at all levels in the services and branches of the Vietnam People's Army. This lesson enables students to approach the system of military uniforms and wearing regulations.II. TEXTUniform of the Vietnam People's Army (VPA) is a system of uniforms for soldiers and officers at all levels in the service branches and branches of VPA.Faced with the specific requirements of military operations and building the VPA in the new revolutionary period, gradually modernizing and integrating into the world, the Ministry of National Defense has repeatedly proposed policies.                Currently, our military uniforms are specified in detail: usual uniform, ceremonial uniform, combat uniforms, uniform for each military zone, arm, forces and specific characteristics of each person on duty. Uniforms of the VPA are called according to the names used for each type of uniform; consists of:1. Ceremonial Uniforms2. Usual uniforms3. Combat uniforms4. Uniforms of service and work clothes.Commanders of agencies and units must strictly abide by the regulations of the Ministry of National Defense; military uniforms of different styles and colors are not allowed to be used; regulations on wearing and using military uniforms contrary to regulations.Wearing uniforms must be following each type, each season and only military uniforms and costumes produced and distributed by the army may be used. Do not use military uniforms as plain clothes. Officers and Warrant officers outside working hours, when not on duty, and when participating in activities outside, are allowed to wear plain clothes.            The VPA uniform has contributed to the improvement of military posture and working style, demonstrating the qualities of the "Uncle Ho's soldier" of the people, by the people, and for the people. In international relations, our military uniforms have integrated with the armies of other countries in the world in terms of aesthetics, elegance, power, and modernity.Since the establishment of our Army until now, the uniform of the army has changed a lot, continuously improved in terms of design, color, and material... but never fully equipped, unified, and modern as it is today. K.08 officer uniforms together with K.03 and K.07 soldiers' uniforms have created a beauty, meeting the requirements of building an increasingly regular and modern army in the new period.III. GRAMMAR* Present perfect tensea) UseEg: Since then, Vietnam has surmounted countless difficulties and challenges to firmly maintain independence, reunify the country, and obtain many proud development achievements. (It’s outside the port now.)Has the political instructor been here? - The Present perfect tense expresses an experience as part of someone’s life. “Ever” and “Never” are common with this use. Eg: I have never seen a fixed pitch propeller.       I have travelled a lot in South Sudan.        Have you ever been in a car crash?- The present perfect expresses an action or a state which began in the past and continues to the present. Eg: I have known Alice for six years.How long have you worked as a teacher in the Vietnam Coast Guard education and training centre? Note: the time expressions “for” and “since” are common with this use. We use “for” with a period of time, and “since” with a point in time. Eg: We have lived here for two years. (a period of time)I have not met my comrades since I left the army. (a point in time)b) Form - Positive: S + have/ has +V(PII)Note: The past participle of regular verbs ends in “-ed”. UNIT 3: VIETNAM COAST GUARDI. INTRODUCTIONThe Vietnam Coast Guard shall be a people's armed force and a specialised force of the State. The lesson  gives an overview of general issues about the history of formation, position and functions; principles of organization and operation; mission; authority; scope of operation; organizational system; equipment.II. TEXT* Overview of formation history, location, functionThe establishment of the Vietnam Coast GuardVietnam Coast Guard was established on August 28, 1998, under Decision No. 1069/1998/QĐ-BQP of the Minister of National Defense on the establishment of the Vietnam Marine Police (the predecessor of the Vietnam Coast Guard Command). The Vietnam Coast Guard shall be a people's armed force and a specialised force of the State, playing core roles in enforcing laws, and protecting national security, order and safety at sea. The Vietnam Coast Guard shall perform the function of counseling the Minister of National Defence to promulgate, according to his/her competence, or to make recommendations to the Party and the State on the policies and laws on the protection of national security, order and safety at sea; protecting state sovereignty, sovereignty rights and jurisdiction in the territorial waters of  Vietnam; managing security, order and safety, as well as ensuring the observance of Vietnamese laws, international treaties and conventions to which the Socialist Republic of Vietnam is a contracting party, or international agreements within its competence (in Article 3 of the Law on Vietnam Coast Guard 2018).Principles of organization and operation of the Vietnam Coast GuardBeing put under the absolute and direct leadership in all aspects of the Communist Party of Vietnam, the overall command of the State President, the unified State management of the Government,  and the direct command and administration of the Minister of National Defence. Abiding by the Constitution and laws of Vietnam, as well as international treaties and conventions to which the Socialist Republic of Vietnam is a contracting party. Being organised in a centralised, unified and hierarchical manner from the Vietnam Coast Guard’s Command to grassroots level units. Acting on its own initiative in preventing, detecting combating, handling and penalising the law violations. Combining the missions of protecting sate sovereign, sovereign rights and jurisdiction, and managing security, order and safety at sea with those of marine economic development. Relying upon the people, promote the people’s strength and be put under their supervision (in Article 4 of the Law on Vietnam Coast Guard 2018).A Vietnam Coast Guard sqaudron on patrolMissions of the Vietnam Coast GuardCollecting information, analyzing, evaluating and forecasting the situation so as to recommend advocacy, solutions and plans for national security protection and law enforcement at sea; studying, analysing, forecasting and counseling the authorities to promulgate policies and legislation on the protection ò national sovereignty, sovereign rights, jurisdiction and national security in the territorial waters of Vietnam; securing order and safety; preventing and combating crimes and law violations at sea (in Article 8 of the Law on Vietnam Coast Guard 2018).Vietnam Coast Guard  conducting combat readiness trainingAuthority of the Vietnam Coast GuardMaking a record of violating shipsPatrolling, inspecting and controlling people, vessels, cargo and luggage in the territorial waters of Vietnam under the provisions of this law and other relevant law provisions.Using weapons, explosives and supporting tools. Using professional technical means and equipment. Imposing legal penalties for administrative violations based on law provisions for administrative violation penalties. Conducting a number of criminal investigation activities in accordance with the law on the organisation of criminal investigation agencies and criminal procedure law.Chasing vessels with law violations at sea.Mobilising people, vessels and civil technical means and equipment of Vietnamese offices, organisations and citizens in case of emergency.Requesting foreign organisations and individuals operating in the territorial waters of Vietnam to provide support and assistance in case of emergencies.Arresting seagoing vessels as regulated by law. Appling working measures prescribed by this Law (in Article 9 of the Law on Vietnam Coast Guard 2018).Scope of operation performed by the Vietnam Coast Guard.The Vietnam Coast Guard shall operate in the territorial waters of Vietnam to perform its functions, missions and authority as regulated this Law. In the case of serving for humanitarian or peaceful purposes, combating, preventing and controlling crimes and law violations, the Vietnam Coast Guard may operate outside the territorial waters of Vietnam; while on duty, it shall be required to comply with the laws of Vietnam, international treaties and conventions to which the Socialist Republic of Vietnam is a contracting party, and international agreements related to the functions, missions and authority of the Vietnam Coast Guard (in Article 11 of the Law on Vietnam Coast Guard 2018).* Organizational system of the Vietnam Coast Guard1. The organizational system of the Vietnam Coast Guard includes: the Vietnam Coast Guard High Command; Coast Guard Regional Command and units directly under the Vietnam Coast Guard High Command (the 1st Coast Guard Regional Command, the 2nd Coast Guard Regional Command, the 3rd Coast Guard Regional Command, the 4th Coast Guard Regional Command; No. 1 Narcotics Prevention Base; No. 2 Narcotics Prevention Base; No. 3 Narcotics Prevention Base; No. 4 Narcotics Prevention Base, No. 1 Reconnaissance Base, No. 2 Reconnaissance Base; Vietnam Coast Guard training and education center and Grassroots level units). (Article 7 of Decree No. 61/2019/ND-CP dated July 10, 2019, of the Government detailing some articles and measures to implement the Vietnam Coast Guard Law).2. Operational scope and management area:+ The 1st Regional Coast Guard Command manages the waters from Bac Luan estuary in Quang Ninh province to Con Co island in Quang Tri province;+ The 2nd Regional Coast Guard Command manages the waters from Con Co island in Quang Tri province to Cu Lao Xanh in Binh Dinh province;+ The 3rd Regional Coast Guard Regional manages the waters from Cu Lao Xanh, Binh Dinh province to the north shore of Dinh An estuary, Tra Vinh province;+ The 4th Regional Coast Guard Regional manages the waters from the north shore of Dinh An estuary in Tra Vinh province to Ha Tien in Kien Giang province.The Operational scope and management area of No. 1 Narcotics Prevention Base; No. 2 Narcotics Prevention Base; No. 3 Narcotics Prevention Base; No. 4 Narcotics Prevention Base, No. 1 Reconnaissance Base, No. 2 Reconnaissance Base is regulated by the Vietnam Coast Guard Commandant.* Equipment of the Vietnam Coast GuardThe Vietnam Coast Guard ship 8002 and Coast Guard ship 8003 jointly patrol the seaThe Vietnam Coast Guard shall be equipped with vessels, boats, aircraft and other means; weapons, explosives, supporting tools, and other technical and professional equipment for implementing the assigned functions, missions and authority ( in Article 33 of the Law on Vietnam Coast Guard 2018).With a spirit of being positive, proactive, not afraid of danger, and ready to overcome big waves and storms, ships of the Vietnam Coast Guard have successfully carried out hundreds of rescues and saved the property of fishermen in distress in far - away sea. The Vietnam Coast Guard always identifies and accompanies fishermen, search and rescue at sea as a combat duty in peacetime, a "heart command", contributing to building the image of officers and soldiers: persistent, close to fishermen, and propagating the law. The presence of the Vietnam Coast Guard at sea, especially on distant seas, has become a belief, a solid fulcrum for fishermen to firmly reach out to sea, contributing to the course of building the entire people’s national defense posture, and the people's security posture at sea.III. GRAMMAR*GerundA gerund is a verb in its “ing” (present participle) form that functions as a noun that names an activity rather than a person or thing. Any action verb can be made into a gerund.Eg: The missions of the Vietnam Coast Guard are collecting information, analyzing, evaluating and forecasting the situation to propose guidelines, solutions and plans for national security protection and law enforcement at seaOne of the powers of the Vietnam Coast Guard is mobilizing people, ships and civil technical means and equipment of Vietnamese agencies, organizations and citizens in case of emergency.- Gerunds can appear at the beginning of a sentence when used as a subject:Eg: Preserving sovereignty, sovereign rights and jurisdiction of the country in the waters of Vietnam is a duty of our unit.- Gerunds can act as an object following the verb:Eg: Daniel quit smoking a year ago.- Gerunds can serve as an object after a preposition:Eg: This unit specializes in analyzing military intelligence data.- Some verbs and verb phrases are directly followed by a gerund:Eg: The authority avoids using nuclear weapons in wars.- Some verbs can be followed by a gerund or an infinitive without causing a change in meaning:Eg: Some people prefer getting up early in the morning. content_md: UNIT 1:  STIPULATING THE LAW RELATED TO FUNCTIONS, MISSIONS AND AUTHORITY OF THE VIETNAM COAST GUARD.I. INTRODUCTIONThe Vietnam Coast Guard law prescribes the status, functions, missions, authority, organisation and operation of the Vietnam Coast Guard; benefits and other policies for the Vietnam Coast Guard; responsibilities of offices, organisations and individuals involved.Parade of the Vietnam Coast GuardII. TEXTThe Law on Vietnam Coast Guard was passed by the 14th National Assembly at its 6th Session, on November 19, 2018; Effective from 1/7/2019, including 8 chapters, and 41 articles. The Law concretizes the provisions of the 2013 Constitution, ensuring consistency with the Vietnamese legal system and following international treaties to which the Socialist Republic of Vietnam is a contracting party. The content of the Law clearly stipulates functions, missions, authority, organisation and operation of the Vietnam Coast Guard; benefits and other policies for the Vietnam Coast Guard; responsibilities of offices, organisations and individuals involved. In which, the most important is the regulation that the Vietnam Coast Guard shall be a people’s armed force and specialised force of the State, playing core roles in enforcing laws, and protecting national security, order and safety at sea. The introduction of the Law on the Vietnam Coast Guard is an important step toward perfecting the Vietnamese legal system for the management and protection of national seas and islands. At the same time, it is a strong statement of the Vietnamese Party and Nation about their determination to protect national interests, protect sovereignty, sovereign rights, and national jurisdiction at sea by legal, civil, and peaceful measures. The law creates an open and convenient legal corridor for the Vietnam Coast Guard to perform the functions and tasks assigned by the Party, State, and People. At the same time, the Law also creates a legal basis to invoke and explain the legitimacy and representation of the state by the Vietnam Coast Guard, ensuring its similarity with the legislative practice of many countries in the region and the world (has its own rules).In terms of Vietnamese law, the Law on Vietnam Coast Guard details and concretizes the tasks and powers of the Vietnam Coast Guard scattered in some laws such as the Law on National Border, 2003; Law on National Security, 2004; Law on Vietnam Sea, 2012; Law on Handling of Administrative Violations, 2012; Law on Customs, 2014; Law on Protection of Natural Resources, Environment and Islands 2014, Law on Organization of Criminal Investigation Agency 2015, Law on Vietnam Maritime Code, 2015; Law on Criminal Procedure Code, 2015; Law on Criminal Code, 2015, Law on Fisheries, 2017; Law on National Defense, 2018…In terms of international law, the Law on the Vietnam Coast Guard ensures compatibility and compliance with the provisions of international law, including the 1982 United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, the Convention on the maritime network in 1974, amended and supplemented in 1978 – SOLAS 1974; the Convention for the Prevention of Unlawful Acts Against the Safety of Navigation (SUA 88) and the Protocol for the Prevention of Unlawful Acts against the Safety of Navigation in respect of fixed drilling rigs on the continental shelf geography; Convention on Search and Rescue at Sea 1979 (SAR 19979); Regional Cooperation Agreement on Combating Piracy and Armed Robbery Against Ships in Asia…The Law of Vietnam Coast Guard was formulated and promulgated to meet the inevitable and necessary requirements of building a force as the core of law enforcement, protecting national security, order, and safety at sea in Vietnam in the new situation. The Law is the document with the highest legal effect, of special importance and political significance for the Vietnam Coast Guard in its organization, operation, and future development. The synchronous and complete implementation of the Vietnam Coast Guard Law is a key task of all levels and sectors in general, and the Vietnam Coast Guard in particular, to improve the efficiency of management and protection of Vietnamese marine areas by activities to ensure law enforcement, administrative handling, and civil nature to match the trend of settling disputes and disagreements between countries by peaceful measures, following the Charter of the United Nations in 1945.III. GRAMMAR*Modal verbsa) UseThe modal verbs include can, must, may, might, will, would, and should. They are used with other verbs to express ability, obligation, possibility, and so on. Below is a list showing the most useful modals and their most common meanings:ModalMeaningExamplecanto express abilityI can speak a little Russian.canto request permissionCan I open the window?mayto express possibilityI may be home late.mayto request permissionMay I sit down, please?mustto express obligationI must go now.mustto express a strong beliefShe must be over 90 years old.shouldto give adviceYou should stop smoking.wouldto request or offerWould you like a cup of tea?wouldin if-sentencesIf I were you, I would say sorry.b) Form A modal verb is followed by another verb in the base form (the infinitive without the 'To') and they are not conjugated (we don't add an 'S' in third person). - Positive: S + modal verb + V(infinitive)Eg: The commander can decide on the quantity, composition, equipment, ships and boats of the force.       When patrolling, inspecting and controlling, the Vietnam Coast Guard ships must display the colors of their ships, badges, identification marks and uniform- Negative: S + modal verb + not + V (infinitive)Eg: Foreign ships must not illegally enter Vietnam's waters.      Vietnam Coast Guard cannot stop the ship without detecting signs of law violation- Interrogative: Modal verb + S + V(infinitive) ? Eg: Must I take pilot?      May I know the location of the ship in distress? IV. INTRODUCTION Maritime is an industry code which specializes in training and providing expertise and knowledge for officers of the Vietnam Navy and the Vietnam Coast Guard. The following lecture will introduce readers to the practical operation of the Vietnam Coast Guard navigation section and the training codes of the VietnamCoast Guard.Navigating ship at seaII. TEXTVessels of Vietnamese nationality, including Vietnam Coast Guard ships and public service ships, are governed by the provisions of the Vietnam Maritime Code (2015), the maritime training sector specified in the Education Law and other detailed regulatory documents, and implementation guidelines of the Government, the Prime Minister and relevant ministries and branches.The navigation section is a profession that specializes in training and providing expertise and knowledge for officers of the Vietnamese Navy, Vietnam Coast Guard, and crew members on the provisions of Vietnamese law and international law on the sea, maritime rules, maritime signal system, responsibilities, and obligations of the commanding officer and crew members, marine safety equipment, hydrometeorology, ship engineering; and carrying people and carrying goods at sea. The navigation section is one of the most important training industries not only for Vietnam but also for any maritime country in the world.The Vietnam Coast Guard is invested by the state in ships, aircraft, weapons, and technical equipment and prioritizes the application of modern science and technology. Stemming from the multi-functional, multi-tasking nature and the very wide range of activities of the Vietnam Coast Guard following the law, it is very important to ensure the work of the Vietnam Coast Guard directly affects the synergy of the force and the ability to perform tasks at sea.Although the law has not yet regulated Coast Guard Navigation training (Coast Guard section). However, in practice, the training section of the Coast Guard, Coast Guard Navigation, includes:- Own and exploit, safely and effectively operate technical equipment in the navigation industry such as: Magnetic compass, Gyro compass, Digital compass; Hydraulic steering system; Ship steering system and Autopilot; Automatic working machines; Road calculator; Depth gauge; Navigation radar; Electronic charts (EC); Global Positioning System GPS; Integrated marine systems (IMS)…; coordinate and cooperate with other branches on the ship to perform well the tasks.- Optimal itinerary planning. Locate the ship and track the ship's path using different methods. Analyze, evaluate, and handle to ensure navigation safety for ships at all times and in different seagoing conditions.- Calculation of maneuvering operations and navigation security for ships when using weapons in combat, performing information, technical, surveying, and other tasks.- Organization of branch command in combat preparation, sea preparation, seafaring, and combat; implementing training regimes.- Organize and command the branch to implement the regimes of preservation, maintenance, and repair of weapons and technical equipment according to decentralization.The officers and soldiers of the Vietnam Coast Guard need to regularly receive additional training, fostering and impart seafaring experience, especially young officers and sailors who are new to the ship's regulations in narrow channels with limited visibility; regulations on operation on the seas, the law of the sea and Law on maritime navigation safety... to improve professional qualifications, contribute to firmly protecting the sovereignty, sovereign rights, and jurisdiction of the country, protect the rights and interests of organizations and individuals lawfully operating at sea.III. content_md: UNIT 3: PROFESSION OF THE VIETNAM COAST GUARDI. INTRODUCTIONThe lecture introduces the working measures of the Vietnam Coast Guard, which is how the force is organized to perform its functions, missions and authority. The reality of the need to increase the use of the Coast Guard in the management and protection of sea areas as well as the internal requirements for the force's construction and development have set an urgent requirement to develop and apply working measures. in organizing the performance of functions and duties of the Coast Guard.Checking violated oil tanker on the seaII. TEXTWorking measures of the Coast Guard are determined and applied based on political tasks; The functions, tasks and authority are prescribed by law and require the management and protection of sea areas of the Coast Guard.After nearly 25 years of operation, the practice has proved that the measures of the Coast Guard have their characteristics and are effectively implemented by the Vietnam Coast Guard in protecting sovereignty, and maintaining security and order. , safe at sea.However, before the Law on Coast Guard of Vietnam, measures for the work of the Coast Guard in particular, theoretical issues about the Coast Guard, in general, have not been properly researched and developed; not yet recognized by law, regulated or regulated incompletely.To institutionalize the working measures of the Coast Guard to protect national security, and ensure order and safety at sea by the law, the Vietnam Coast Guard Law 2018 specifically stipulates 7 working measures of the Coast Guard in Article 12, Section I, Chapter III, which are: (1) Mass mobilization, (2) Law, (3) Diplomacy, (4) Economic, (5) ) Scientific-technical, (6) Professional, (7) Armed measure to defend national security and to secure order and safety at sea as regulated in this law.Currently, according to the provisions of current law, related to the use of the above working measures, the 2004 National Security Law stipulates a specialized force to protect national security (including the National Security Police). Vietnam's coast guard) may use the above 07 measures to protect national security. The Government has issued 02 Decrees on mass mobilization and legal measures.To ensure an effective fight against all types of crimes and violations of the law in the field of order and safety at sea, it is necessary to advise competent authorities to issue legal documents on the issue of maritime security. professional measures. However, human rights and citizens' rights may be restricted only under the provisions of the law in case of necessity for reasons of national defence, national security, social order and safety, social morality, etc. community health (according to Clause 2, Article 14 of the 2013 Constitution). Meanwhile, if it is necessary to publicize the provisions on professional measures of the Law, it will likely reveal professional secrets, affecting the effectiveness of the fight against crime and law violations.The specific and clear regulation of Coast Guard working measures in the Vietnam Coast Guard Law is a new point compared to the Ordinance on the Vietnam Coast Guard. This new point not only contributes to overcoming the shortcomings of the previous legal system but also serves as a solid legal basis for the Vietnam Coast Guard to carry out its assigned functions, tasks and powers. ; properly demonstrate its position and role as the people's armed forces, the State's specialized force, as the core of law enforcement at sea.III. content_md: UNIT 4: PATROL, INSPECTION, AND CONTROL OF THEVIETNAM COAST GUARDI. INTRODUCTIONThe process of patrolling, checking and controlling is the sequence of steps performed by officers and soldiers of the Vietnam Coast Guard's patrol, inspection and control force since the signal to stop ships is issued for inspection, board the vessel to be inspected until the inspection and control activities are completed and leave the inspected and controlled vessel.A Vietnam Coast Guard ship on patrolII. TEXTAccording to the functions, mission, authority of the Vietnam Coast Guard as prescribed in the Law on Vietnam Coast Guard 2018, at the request of the Commandant of the Vietnam Coast Guard, dated February 11, 2019, The Minister of National Defense issued Circular No. 15/2019/TT-BQP stipulating the patrol, inspection and control process of the Vietnam Coast Guard.Coordinating with Hai Phong Police to apprehend a copper ore smugglingDuring patrolling, inspection and control, when detecting violations, the Coast Guard has the right to handle violations following the law. Regarding this content, Article 19, Circular No. 15/2019/TT-BQP guides as follows:1. When detecting signs of administrative law violation, the inspection and control team must promptly prevent and immediately stop the violation and explain to the violator about the violation, rights and obligations according to the regulations of the Law.2. The head of the inspection and control team shall make minutes of violations and issue decisions on sanctioning administrative violations according to their competence as prescribed by law.3. In case the administrative violation is not belong to the sanctioning competence, the head of the inspection and control team shall make working records, and minutes of violations, and apply measures to prevent and collect violations. collect documents and evidence according to their competence and immediately report to the commander of the patrol, inspection and control force.4. The commanders of patrol, inspection and control forces shall issue decisions to sanction administrative violations according to their competence or based on the nature of the cases, and promptly report them to the competent superior commanders for organization. escorting vessels in violation, applying preventive measures and taking measures to verify, investigate and conclude the case.5. In case an offender is found in the act, a person is wanted or sought, officers and soldiers of the Vietnam Coast Guard who are on duty to inspect and control shall take measures as prescribed. by the law on the organization of criminal investigation agencies and the law on criminal procedure.(Excerpt from Article 19, Circular No. 15/2019/TT-BQP stipulating the patrol, inspection and control process of the Vietnam Coast Guard). The patrol, inspection, and control operations of the Vietnam Coast Guard play a crucial role in safeguarding Vietnam's coastal areas, territorial waters, and exclusive economic zone. These operations are aimed at maintaining maritime security, enforcing laws and regulations, protecting marine resources, and ensuring the safety of navigation.Patrols conducted by the Vietnam Coast Guard involve the deployment of vessels and aircraft to monitor and surveil the country's maritime domain. These patrols cover a wide range of activities, including maritime surveillance, search and rescue operations, and law enforcement. By maintaining a visible presence at sea, the Vietnam Coast Guard deters illegal activities, responds swiftly to incidents, and protects the sovereignty and integrity of Vietnam's waters.Inspection activities carried out by the Vietnam Coast Guard involve the examination of vessels, both domestic and foreign, to ensure compliance with maritime laws and regulations. Inspections are conducted to verify the validity of licenses and permits, check for adherence to safety standards, prevent smuggling and illegal activities, and enforce fisheries regulations. Through thorough inspections, the Vietnam Coast Guard seeks to maintain order, protect the marine environment, and uphold the rule of law at sea.Control measures implemented by the Vietnam Coast Guard involve monitoring and regulating the movement of vessels within Vietnamese waters. This includes controlling maritime traffic, conducting port security operations, and regulating the entry and exit of vessels in sensitive areas. By exercising control, the Vietnam Coast Guard aims to prevent unauthorized activities, enforce maritime boundaries, and ensure the safety and security of ports and coastal infrastructure.The patrol, inspection, and control operations of the Vietnam Coast Guard are carried out in coordination with other relevant agencies, such as the Navy, Fisheries Surveillance, and Customs, as well as with international partners. These operations contribute to maintaining maritime order, protecting national interests, and supporting the sustainable development of Vietnam's marine resources. The Vietnam Coast Guard's dedication to patrol, inspection, and control activities underscores its commitment to maritime safety, security, and the rule of law in Vietnamese waters.III. GRAMMAR1. Must a) Use- “Must” expresses strong obligation. Generally, this obligation comes from inside the speaker.Eg: I must get my hair cut. (I think this is necessary) - Because “must” expresses the authority of the speaker, you should be careful of using “You must…”. It sounds very bossy. Eg: You must help me. (I’m giving you an order). - “Must” can expresses a strong suggestion. Eg: You must give a ring when you are next in town. b) Form- Positive:S + must + V(infinitive) + (O)Eg: I must try harder.      She must study more. - Negative: S + must + not +  V(infinitive) + (O)Contraction: must not = mustn’t Eg: You mustn’t steal anything.         They mustn’t enter that room.  - Interrogative: Must + S + V(infinitive)?- Yes, S + must.- No, S + must + not.Eg: Must I take exams? Yes, you must.        Do I have to the exam? Yes, you do.Note: Questions with “must” are possible, but the use of “have to” is more common. 2. Have to a) Use- “Have to” expresses strong obligation. The obligation comes from outside – perhaps a law, a rule at school or work or someone in authority.Eg: You have to have a driving license if you want to drive a car.        The doctor says I have to do more exercise. - “Don’t/ doesn’t have to” expresses absence of obligation (it isn’t necessary).Eg: You don’t have to do the washing up. I’ve got a dishwasher.        She doesn’t have to work on Monday. It’s her day off.  b) Form- Positive:S + have/ has to + V(infinitive) + (O)Note: I/ we/ you/ they + have          She/ he/ it + hasEg: I have to learn English.      She has to obey the rules.- Negative: S + do/ does + not +  V(infinitive) + (O)Eg: I don’t have to work hard.         She doesn’t have to work hard.   - Interrogative: Do/ does + S + have to + V(infinitive)?- Yes, S + do/ does.- No, S + do/ does + not.Eg: Do you have to wear uniform? Yes, I do. No, he doesn’t.- Wh-question: Wh + do/does + S + have to + V(infinitive)?Eg: What does she have to do now? - Note: The past tense of “have to” is “had to”, with “did” and “didn’t” in the question and the negative. content_md: UNIT 5: CRIME FIGHTING AND PREVENTION UNDER THE JURISDICTION OF THE VIETNAM COAST GUARDI. INTRODUCTIONFighting against crime and breaking the law is one of the specific functions and tasks of the Vietnam Coast Guard. The following lecture will introduce practical requirements, operational results, and measures to improve operational efficiency in the upcoming time.Checking violated oil tanker on the seaII. TEXTIn Vietnamese waters, the Vietnam Coast Guard has the function of managing security, order, and safety and ensuring the observance of Vietnam's laws, and international treaties to which the Socialist Republic of Vietnam is a signatory and international agreement under its jurisdiction. In case for the purpose of religious education, peace, crime prevention, and law violations, the Vietnam Coast Guard may operate outside Vietnamese waters.With the tradition of "Resolutely brave, overcome difficulties, unite, synergize, strictly abide by the law", over the years, Vietnam Coast Guard officers and soldiers have made unremitting efforts to build and perfect, fostering the core values of the Vietnam Coast Guard soldier: "Responsibility - Discipline - Righteousness".In recent years, the global and regional situation, especially the situation in the East Sea, has become complicated and unpredictable, with many new situations appearing in both traditional and non-traditional security aspects. In terms of traditional security, there are disputes over sovereignty over sea and islands and maritime delimitation (bilateral and multilateral) among countries along the East Sea. In terms of non-traditional security, there is an increase in organized and transnational crimes related to drugs, arms trafficking, human trafficking, smuggling, commercial fraud, piracy, terrorism, armed robbery against ships, and climate change (sea level rise) natural disasters, unusual storms, epidemics, the marine environment pollution.In addition to patrolling, inspection, control, and law enforcement activities to protect sovereignty, sovereign rights, and national jurisdiction, and protect organizations and individuals participating in marine economic development activities; another important function of the Vietnam Coast Guard is to fight against crimes and law violations in Vietnamese waters to maintain security, order, and safety at sea.Stemming from the trend of international cooperation of countries in the world today is to implement the policy of expanding international relations, giving priority to the direction of the sea; along with the advantages of the 4.0 technology revolution, organized crime organizations, transnational (regional, global) have rapidly expanded their scope and operational area with increasingly dangerous methods. Their scope of impact is not only limited to the region but also on a global scale. To effectively combat such international crimes at sea, a single country cannot do well but needs the practical cooperation of many countries and international institutions in the regions and around the world.Vietnam Coast Guard is a law enforcement force representing Vietnam operating in Vietnamese waters and international waters; uses the seal bearing the national emblem to perform assigned functions and tasks. To improve the effectiveness of the fight against crime and law violations at sea, the Vietnam Coast Guard has promoted international relations activities in both breadth and depth, establishing hotlines with the Coast Guard Law Enforcement in 09 countries in the region; establishing strong cooperative relations with partner countries of ASEAN, many maritime powers and international organizations in the world in the field of maintaining security, order, and safety at sea.Checking violated oil tanker on the seaThe above contents can be clearly seen through the practice of fighting against smuggling, commercial fraud, and illegal transportation of goods at sea. The Vietnam Coast Guard has implemented many solutions synchronously, including closely coordinating with Vietnamese functional forces (Border Guards, Police, Customs, Maritime Inspectors, Market Managers, etc..) and neighboring countries (Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines, China, Cambodia, Thailand...); collect, share information, grasp the situation, strengthen patrol, inspection, and control in key sea areas; promote and improve the quality and efficiency of coordination in organizing professional activities, proactively detecting, promptly preventing and fighting crimes of smuggling, commercial fraud, and illegal transportation of goods at sea. During the deployment process, the Vietnam Coast Guard at the same time promoted propaganda, popularized legal education for fishermen, and participated in building the people's security posture associated with the all-people national defense posture to protect the country's sovereignty over sea and islands, effectively serving the course of sustainable development of Vietnam's marine economy in the new situation.III. GRAMMAR*Conditional sentences type 1a) Use - The Conditional sentence type 1 is used to express a possible condition and a probable in the future. Eg: If I study hard, I will pass this exam.        If she has enough money, she will buy a new car. - Note: + English uses a present tense in the condition clause, not a future form. Eg: If this ship enters the harbour,…(not If this ship will enter the harbour) + “If” expresses a possibility that something will happen. “When” expresses what the speaker sees as certain to happen.Eg: If I find the pilot chart, I’ll send it to you.       When the fire team is ready, we’ll rope off the fire area. b) Form- Positive and negative: If + S + V (present simple), S + will/ won’t + V (infinitive)Eg: If we transmit an alarm signal to vessels in the vicinity, all the vessels have to pay attention.        If you are late, I won’t wait for you. - Interrogative: Will + S + V(infinitive) + if + S + V (present simple)?Eg: Will you attend Australian Defence Force Academy if you pass your exam? Yes, I will. - Wh-question: Wh + will + S + V(infinitive) + if + S + V(present simple)?Eg: What will you do if you attend Australian Defence Force Academy? - Note: The conditional clause “if” can come at the beginning of the sentence or at the end. If it comes at the beginning, we put a comma at the end of the clause. If it comes at the end, we don’t use a comma. Eg: If he studies hard, he’ll pass this exam.                  He’ll pass this exam if he studies hard.IV. content_md: UNIT 6: COMMUNICATION ON THE VIETNAM COAST GUARD SHIPI. INTRODUCTIONThe communication on the Vietnam Coast Guard ship is decisive for the completion of any sea voyage. The following lecture will introduce readers to the purposes and forms of communication on board the Coast Guard ships. Using of communication systems on the Vietnam Coast Guard ship.II. TEXTThe communication on the Vietnam Coast Guard ships is for the purpose of conveying the commander's orders to combat positions to perform regular duties as well as unscheduled missions. In particular, the communication on the Vietnam Coast Guard ships also transmits reports of violations detected to the headquarters.Communication can be compared to the circulating blood vessels connecting all activities of Vietnam Coast Guard ships. In addition to bearing the general characteristics of the communications industry in the whole army, it is worthy of the golden words that Uncle Ho commended for "timely-accurate-confidential-safe". The communication on the Vietnam Coast Guard ship also has a more extensive feature in the scope, fields, objects, options and solutions for law enforcement in many situations, in many sea areas with different legal regulations.The communication on the Vietnam Coast Guard ships is for the purpose of conveying the commander's orders to combat positions to perform regular duties as well as unscheduled missions. In particular, the communication on the Coast Guard ships also transmits reports of violations detected to the headquarters (commonly handling violations, seeking guidance when there are violations beyond the normal handling capacity). There are many forms of communication on board the Vietnam Coast Guard ships currently in common use, with three main forms:MorseHand flagsMoose lightsDepending on the case and the level of urgency, the direct commander on board will order the communication staff to use the appropriate form of communication to transmit confidentially, quickly, and accurately.The communication on board the Vietnam Coast Guard ships is decisive for the completion of all missions at sea. In any situation, communication needs to be guaranteed to be transparent because it requires high "combat independence" accuracy and timeliness. Communication like blood vessels inseparable from a healthy body, determines the success of any mission.III. GRAMMAR* Imperative verbsImperative verbs are verbs that create an imperative sentence that gives an order or command. a) Form- Positives: V (+ O)Eg: Relax.      Finish your homework.      Take a deep breath.Imperative verbs actually do have a subject, but it is never stated. That subject is “you” (the second-person singular or plural).Imperative verbs are always stated in the simple present. Because the subject is the unstated “you”, the verb form is the simple present, second-person singular form (which looks like a base verb). It never takes an -s (third-person singular) ending.- Negatives:  DO + NOT + V (+ O)Contraction: Do not = Don’t Eg: Do not turn off GPS.      Don’t change to automatic steering.      Don’t work too late.- Questions in English almost always include a subject.Eg:  Do you accept shore-based navigational assistance from the pilot? b) Function- We use imperative verbs to give commands or directions, state rules, or give advice. In fact, the word imperative means commanding, important or controlling.- Remind English language learners that imperative verbs can be directed at one person (the second person singular) or two or more people (the second person plural).- Common uses of imperative verbs include:+ Captains telling the second officer what to do:Eg: Complete your duty!      Hoist the flag signal Oscar and report!      Maintain visual contact with a person in the water!      Don’t navigate by yourself!+ Teachers giving instructions to students:Eg: Finish the exercise on page 8.      Stop talking!      Open your books to Chapter 2.      Don’t look at your phones in class.+ Employers giving instructions to employees:Eg: Hand in that report by Friday.      Don’t forget about the meeting tomorrow.      Turn your computer off when you leave.      Stop by my office.+ People in authority, such as police officers, telling other people what to do:Eg: Don’t drink and drive.      Put all metal objects into this container.      Fill out this form.      Show me your ID.+ Rules, guidelines, or laws:Eg: Don’t run by the pool.      Do not trespass.      Take off your shoes.      Dress appropriately.+ Friends or family members giving advice:Eg: Don’t forget to call him back.      Follow up with an email.IV. INTRODUCTIONThe Vietnam Coast Guard ship’s command stipulates the basic principles, organization and combat preparation work on the Vietnam Coast Guard ship. In this reading, readers will approach the purposes, organizational system, and regulations of the command of the Vietnam Coast Guard ships.Command of the Vietnam Coast Guard shipsII. TEXTIn order to build regularity, practice discipline, and create a common unity in the entire force, all officers and soldiers of the Vietnam Coast Guard while working or participating in work on ships of the Vietnam Coast Guard must strictly abide by the Command of the Vietnam Coast Guard ships.The command of the Vietnam Coast Guard ships regulates the basic principles, organization, and combat preparation work on the Vietnam Coast Guard ships. Thereby, the Vietnam Coast Guard officers and soldiers on the payroll of the Vietnam Coast Guard ships and all other subjects, in general, must understand and perform well some basic requirements on staffing organization, regime, study, and work. Studying and training following the Vietnam Coast Guard ship's Command helps learners improve the efficiency of etiquette, manners, and strict observance, creating a basis for all officers and soldiers on the ship and other subjects to practice and strictly implement responsibilities and duties in all aspects of work; is a premise to return to good work at other ship units later.Depending on the type of ships, there will be payrolls of different branches and combat positions, but basically, the organizational system has many similarities, specifically:- Commanding officer- Political commissar- Head of industry, team leadersThe branches on the ship are organized for the purpose of exploiting and using weapons, equipment and technical equipment to the highest efficiency.Industries on the ship include:- Navigation section, symbol “I”- Weapon system section, symbol “II”- General section, symbol “III”- Communication and rada section, symbol “IV”- Electricity and Engine section, symbol “V”- Military medical crew, symbol “KY”- Flight assurance crew, symbol “KB”.The rescue team on the multi-purpose patrol ship is established when there is a situation and disbanded when the mission is over.The patrol, inspection and control team is established when going to sea and it disbands itself after completing the mission.Besides the branches on the warship, it is possible to organize divisions, and groups, in charge of machines, batteries, and combat positions below the branches.Ships of the Vietnam Coast Guard are a great asset that the Party, the State, the Central Military Commission (CMC), and the Ministry of Defense equip for the Vietnam Coast Guard to perform its assigned functions and tasks; including patrol ships, specialized ships, service ships, boats, and floating facilities. Based on the organization of personnel, weapons, technical equipment and function, duties of the ship, operating range, displacement, technical features, and tactics to decentralize the decentralization prescribed by Commandant of the Vietnam Coast Guard.  The Vietnam Coast Guard ships are classified into 5 levels, the highest being level 1.In addition, the Vietnam Coast Guard Ship Order also stipulates the wearing and use of uniforms, professional attire, and aircraft on the Vietnam Coast Guard ships, general regulations when boarding and disembarking ships, and regulations on professional law work, international relations, logistics, and technical work on the Vietnam Coast Guard ships.III. GRAMMAR1. Imperative sentence  - An imperative sentence gives advice or instructions; it can also express a request or command. These kinds of sentences are also known as directives because they provide direction to whoever is being addressed.- Types of Imperative Sentences: Directives can take one of several forms in everyday speech and writing. A few of the most common uses include:+ A request: Pack enough clothing for the cruise.+ An invitation: Come by at 8, please.+ A command: Raise your hands and turn around.+ An instruction: Turn left at the intersection.Imperative sentences can be confused with other kinds of sentences. The trick is to look at how the sentence is constructed.- “You” are the SubjectImperative sentences may seem to have no subject, but the implied subject is you, or, as it is properly called, you understood. The proper way to write the subject is (you) in parenthesis, especially when diagramming an imperative sentence. Even when a proper name is mentioned in an imperative sentence, the subject still is understood.Eg: Jim, close the door before the cat gets out! The subject is (you), not Jim.- Modifying an imperative sentence:At their most basic, imperative sentences are binary, which is to say they must be either positive or negative. Positive imperatives use affirmative verbs in addressing the subject; negatives do the opposite. + Positive: Keep both hands on the steering wheel while you're driving.+ Negative: Don't operate the lawnmower without wearing safety goggles.Adding the words "do" or "just" to the beginning of the sentence, or the word "please" to the conclusion— called softening the imperative —makes imperative sentences more polite or conversational.Softened imperatives: Do your chores, please. Just sit here, won't you?As with other forms of grammar, imperative sentences can be modified to address a particular subject, follow a proprietary written style, or simply add variety and emphasis to your writing.- Adding emphasis: Imperative sentences also can be modified to single out a particular person or to address a group. This can be accomplished in one of two ways: by following the interrogative with a tag question or by closing with an exclamation point.+ Tag question: Shut the door, would you, please?+ Exclamation: Someone, call a doctor!Doing so in both instances adds emphasis and drama to speech and writing.IV. content_md: UNIT 8: DAILY LIFE ON THE VIETNAM COAST GUARD SHIP: CHALLENGES AND REWARDSI. INTRODUCTIONThe Vietnam Coast Guard often has to perform long-term patrol missions at sea. Despite having to work in difficult living conditions, far from their families, officers and soldiers on the Vietnam Coast Guard ship were still determined to successfully complete their assigned tasks. The lesson will introduce the daily life of the crew members on the Vietnam Coast Guard ship while performing their patrol, inspection and control duties.II. TEXT The Vietnam Coast Guard is a branch of the military that performs both civil and military missions. Coast Guard officers and crew members are often stationed on ships that patrol the nation’s waters and respond to emergencies. But what is daily life like on a coast guard ship? How do they balance their professional and personal lives? What are some of the challenges and rewards of serving at sea?Daily life on a the Vietnam Coast Guard ship can vary depending on the type, size, and mission of the vessel. Some ships are larger and have longer patrols, while others are smaller and have shorter patrols. Some ships are deployed for search and rescue, law enforcement, environmental protection, while others are involved in training, research, or maintenance.Maintenance of weapons on board -  Photo:InternetHowever, some common aspects of daily life on the Vietnam Coast Guard ship include:Routine and discipline. The Vietnam Coast Guard members follow a strict schedule of duty rotations, watchstanding, training, drills, inspections, and maintenance. They also have to adhere to rules and regulations regarding uniforms, conduct, and safety. They have to be ready for any situation that may arise at sea, such as storms, fires, collisions, or medical emergencies.Teamwork and friendship.Coast guard members work closely with their shipmates and form strong bonds of friendship and trust. They rely on each other for support, guidance, and assistance. They also have fun together by playing games, watching movies, celebrating holidays, or organizing events. They often develop a sense of pride and loyalty to their ship and their unit.Challenges and hardships.The Vietnam Coast Guard members face many challenges and hardships while serving at sea. They have to deal with long hours, physical demands, stressful situations, and constant changes. They also have to cope with separation from their families and friends, limited communication, isolation, boredom, and homesickness. They may encounter dangers such as hostile forces, pirates, smugglers, terrorists or extreme weather condition on sea.The Vietnam Coast Guard participates in the rescue of foreign ships at seaPhoto: InternetRewards and opportunities. The Vietnam Coast Guard members also enjoy many rewards and opportunities while serving at sea. They get to learn new skills and gain valuable experience. They get to help people in need and protect the environment. They get to make a difference and serve their country.Daily life on the Vietnam Coast Guard ship is not easy, but it can be fulfilling and rewarding for those who choose this career path. The Vietnam Coast Guard members are proud of their service and their contribution to the nation’s security and prosperity.III. GRAMMAR1. Verb patterns 11.1. Verb +to+ infinitiveE.g.They want to buy a new car. I'd like to go abroad.1.2. Verb + -ingE.g. Everyone loves going to parties. He finished reading his book.1.3. Verb + -ing or + to + infinitive with no change in meaningE.g. It began to rain/raining.I continued to work/working in the library.1.4. Verb + preposition + -ingE.g. We're thinking of moving house. I'm looking forward to having more free time.1.5. Like doing and would like to doa) Like doing and love doing express a general enjoyment. E.g. I like working as a teacher = I'm a teacher and I enjoy it.I love dancing = This is one of my hobbies.b) Would like to do and would love to do express a preference now or at a specific time.E.g. I'd like to be a teacher. = When I grow up, I want to be a teacher Thank you. I'd love to dance. = We're at a disco. I'm pleased that you asked me.c) Questions and short answersE.g. Would you like to dance? - Yes, I would. / Yes, I'd love to. Would you like to come for a walk? - Yes, I would. / No, thank you. *Note:No, I wouldn't is not common because it is impolite.2. Future intentions2.1. Willa) UseWill is used:- To express a future decision or intention made at the moment of speaking. E.g. A: It's Jane's birthday.B: Is it? I'll buy her some flowers.- To express an offer.E.g. I'll carry your suitcase.We'll do the washing-up.b) Form- PositiveS + will + Vbare infWill is a modal auxiliary verb. The forms of will are the same for all persons.E.g. She will go to Ho Chi Minh city.- NegativeS+will+not+ Vbare infwill not = won'tE.g. They will not buy that house. He will not send this letter to him.- Yes/No questionWill +S+Vbare inf?Yes, S + willNo, S+ will + notE.g. Will you help me? Yes, I will. /No, I won't.-Wh-questionWh/How + will + S+ Vbare inf?E.g. Where will you go tomorrow? I will go to a wedding party.*Note:"No, I won't" is not common because it is impolite. It means "I don't want to help you."A polite way of saying "no" here is "I'm afraid I can't."2.2. Going toa) UseGoing to is used:- To express a future decision, intention or plan made before the moment of speaking.E.g. She is going to have a birthday party. They are going to stay in Rome.b) Form- PositiveS + am/is/are + going + to + Vbare infE.g. They are going to buy a new house.I am going to have an exam next week.- NegativeS + am/is/are + not + going+ to + Vbare infE.g. I am not going to workShe is not wearing that shirt.- Yes/No questionAm/ Is / Are + S + going + to +  Vinf?Yes, S + am/is/ are.No, S + am/ is/are + not.E.g. Are you going to get married next year? Yes, I am.- Wh-questionWh + am/is/are + S + going + to + Vinf?*Note: The Present Continuous can be used in a similar way for a plan or an arrangement, particularly with the verbs go and come.E.g. She's coming on Friday.I'm going home early tonight.- When we can see or feel now that something is certain to happen in the futurE.g. Look at these clouds. It's going to rain.Watch out! That box is going to fall.- Will or going to?I'm going to make a chicken casserole for dinner.(I decided this morning and bought everything for it).What shall I cook for dinner? Er.... I know! I'll make chicken casserole (I decided at the moment of speaking).IV. content_md: UNIT 9: INTERNATIONAL RELATIONSA. FOREIGN RELATIONS BETWEEN THE VIETNAM COAST GUARD AND OTHER COAST GUARDS IN THE WORLDI. INTRODUCTIONInternational relations are an important task of the Vietnam Coast Guard, contributing to the victory of the mission of protecting our country's sovereignty, sovereign rights and jurisdiction at sea, thereby enhancing the role, position and responsibility of Vietnam as a coastal country to countries in the region and the world. This lesson will introduce the achievements of the Vietnam Coast Guard's foreign affairs in recent years and the direction of implementing external missions in the following years.The Japan Coast Guard ship visits and exchanges with the Vietnam Coast Guard.II. TEXTThe Vietnam Coast guard (VCG) is the young  branch of the Vietnamese People’s Army (VPA) and plays an important role in maintaining security and stability in the country’s exclusive economic zone and continental shelf. The VCG also contributes to the protection of Vietnam’s sovereignty and national interests in the East Sea.To handle with these challenges and enhance its capacity and professionalism, the VCG has actively expanded its foreign relations and international cooperation with other coast guards and maritime law enforcement agencies in the w orld. The VCG has participated in various bilateral and multilateral mechanisms, such as the Heads of Asian Coast Guard Agencies Meeting (HACGAM), the ASEAN Coast Guard Forum (ACGF), the Regional Cooperation Agreement on Combating Piracy and Armed Robbery against Ships in Asia (ReCAAP), and the International Maritime Organization (IMO).The VCG has also established direct ties with many coast guards in the region and beyond, such as Japan, China, India, Australia, South Korea, Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand, Cambodia, Laos, Singapore, Brunei, Myanmar, the Philippines, France, Italy, Russia, Canada, and the United States. The VCG has conducted regular exchanges of visits, dialogues, consultations, joint patrols, exercises, training courses, workshops, seminars, and information sharing with these partners. These activities have helped to build trust, mutual understanding, and coordination among the coast guards in addressing common maritime security issues such as piracy, smuggling, illegal fishing, marine pollution, search and rescue, and humanitarian assistance. The JCG delegation visits Ship 8002 of the Vietnam Coast Guard Region 2 Command. Photo: People’s Army NewspaperThe ICG young officers listening to briefing of 2500-nautical mile voyage of the Vietnam Coast Guard ship form Vung Tau to Chennai port. Photo: People’s Army Newspaper.The U.S. Coast Guard Rear Adm. Michael J. Haycock during the handover ceremony of a former Coast Guard Cutter to the Vietnam Coast Guard.One of the most notable examples of VCG’s foreign relations and international cooperation is its partnership with the US coast guard (USCG), which has been strengthened in recent years as part of the US-Vietnam comprehensive partnership. The USCG has provided various forms of support to the VCG, such as transferring two former USCG cutters to the VCG under the Excess Defense Articles program, providing training and equipment for maritime law enforcement, conducting joint patrols and professional exchanges, and facilitating VCG’s articipation in regional forums such as HACGAM and ACGF. The US- Vietnam Coast guard cooperation has contributed to enhancing Vietnam’s maritime domain awareness and sovereignty protection as well as promoting regional stability and security.The VCG’s foreign relations and international cooperation have not only improved its own capabilities and performance but also reflected Vietnam’s active and responsible role in regional and global affairs. The VCG has demonstrated its commitment to upholding international law and norms, especially the 1982 United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), and to cooperating with other coast guards for a peaceful and prosperous maritime environment. The VCG’s foreign relations and international cooperation are expected to continue and deepen in the future as Vietnam pursues its vision of becoming a strong maritime nation.B. THE FIRST “VIETNAM COAST GUARD AND FRIENDS” PROGRAM FOR PEACE, FRIENDSHIP, COOPERATION, DEVELOPMENT.I. TEXTFrom 8th to 11th November 2022, the first "Vietnam Coast Guard and Friends" program held in Vietnam with the goal “For secure, safe seas and clean environment". This will be the first time the VCG High Command has held an exchange program with its counterparts from other countries in the region, especially neighboring countries and those that share maritime borders with Vietnam. Foreign organizations that participated in the program include the National Committee for Maritime Security of Cambodia, the Chinese Coast Guard, the Maritime Security Agency of Indonesia, the Maritime Enforcement Agency of Malaysia, the Philippine Coast Guard, and the Maritime Enforcement Command Center of Thailand.The program is aimed at realizing and effectively carrying out diplomatic policies of the Party and the state; as well as resolutions, directives, and plans of the Central Military Commission and the Ministry of National Defense on international integration and defense diplomacy this year and in the coming years. In addition, the program helped enhance mutual understanding, trust, and consensus among maritime law enforcement agencies of countries in their cooperation, thus joining hands to build a peaceful, prosperous, and developed marine area.The VCG has gradually built trusted and stable cooperative relationships with the coast guard forces of many other ASEAN countries. The VCG has also been a contributing member with a high sense of responsibility in multilateral forums in the region and the world as a whole.The "Vietnam Coast Guard and Friends" program held in Ha NoiThe VCG has established partnerships with counterparts in the U.S, China, Japan, South Korea, and India.To date, the VCG has implemented cooperative documents inked with maritime law enforcement agencies of eight countries, including China, the U.S., Japan, South Korea, India, Cambodia, the Philippines, and Indonesia.III. GRAMMARA. PASSIVE VOICE1. Present SimpleS + am/is/are + PII E.g. English is spoken all over the world. Toyota cars are made in Japan.2. Past SimpleS + was/were + PIIE.g.
